title.narrative: Ipas Access to Safe Abortion II
Ipas Access to Safe Abortion II

description.narrative:
Ipas is an internationally recognized NGO that works to advance reproductive justice by expanding access to safe abortion and contraception globally since 50 years back. Over the years, more than 69 000 women and adolescent girls have accessed safe abortion services and 53 000 have received post¬abortion contraception services.
The project has four key objectives that will be achieved before end of 2027: 1. Women and girls have improved access to available, accessible, and acceptable abortion, contraceptive, and SGBV services within Mozambique's health sector. 2. Humanitarian agencies have enhanced capacity to take evidence¬based action to protect SRHR before, during, and after humanitarian crises. 3. Communities reduce the prevalence of harmful gender norms and cultural practices, increase support for SRHR, and refer people to safe SRH services. 4. A national movement for SRHR—led primarily by women and young people— demands accountability from government leaders on SRHR and SGBV, and resists threats to progress.
This will be achieved through advocacy work in various forums, technical support, dialogue with target groups and local communities, training of health staff and upgrading of care facilities.
It is proposed to support a contribution of 190 million SEK during 2023¬2027 of which 98 million SEK will be allocated to Ipas for their programmatic work to achieve goals 1-3, 90 Million SEK to strengthen an established network of local civil society organizations working within the SRHR sphere, including LGBTQI issues, reflected in goal 4 above and 2 Million SEK for midterm review.

Ipas är en internationellt erkänd SRHR¬organisation som sedan 50 år tillbaka arbetar globalt med sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter och tillgång till säkra aborter. Under projektet har mer än 69 000 kvinnor och tonårsflickor fått tillgång till säkra aborter och 53 000 har fått preventivmedel efter abort.
Insatsen har följande mål som förväntas uppnås till 2027: 1. Kvinnor och barn har förbättrad tillgång till säkra aborter, preventivmedel och stödinsatser för sexuellt och könsbaserat våld inom hälso¬ och sjukvårdssystemet i Moçambique. 2. Humanitära aktörer har ökad kapacitet att vidta evidens¬baserade åtgärder för att skydda och tillförsäkra tillgång till SRHR före, i samband med samt efter konfliktrelaterade kriser. 3. Lokalsamhällen har bidragit till att minska omfattningen av skadliga könsrelaterade normer och beteenden, öka förståelsen kring SRHR och hänvisa människor till inrättningar som erbjuder säkra och tillförlitliga SRHR¬tjänster. 4. En nationell SRHR-rörelse, huvudsakligen ledd av kvinnor och ungdomar, som ställer krav på ett rättvist ansvarstagande från regering och myndigheter kring SRHR och sexuellt och könsbaserat våld och som kan stå emot hot mot progressiva framsteg inom SRHR¬ området.
Detta ska uppnås genom påverkansarbete inom olika forum, tekniskt stöd, dialog med målgrupper och lokalsamhällen, utbildning av hälsopersonal och uppgradering av vårdinrättningar.
Totalt föreslås ett stöd på 190 MSEK under åren 2023–2027 varav 98 MSEK fördelas till Ipas för att genomföra verksamhet som leder till ovanstående mål 1-3; 90 MSEK till att stärka ett etablerat nätverk av lokala civilsamhällsorganisationer som arbetar med SRHR, inklusive HBTQI¬frågor, i enlighet med ovan nämnda mål 4; samt 2 MSEK för en halvtidsöversyn.

The primary goal of the project is to build lasting momentum for gender equality and human rights in Mozambique through improved access to and respect for sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), including safe abortion.
Objective 1: Women and girls have improved access to available, accessible, and acceptable abortion, contraceptive, and SGBV services within Mozambique's health sector
Objective 2: Humanitarian agencies have enhanced capacity to take evidence-based action to protect SRHR before, during, and after humanitarian crises
Objective 3: Communities reduce the prevalence of harmful gender norms and cultural practices, increase support for SRHR, and refer people to safe SRH services
Objective 4: A national movement for SRHR led primarily by women and young people demands accountability from government leaders on SRHR and SGBV, and resists threats to progress

title.narrative: Agreement Ipas Access to safe abortion II
Decision on contribution Ipas access to safe abortion II

description.narrative:
Outcome 1: Women and girls have improved access to available, acceptable, and high-quality abortion, contraceptive, and SGBV services within Mozambique's health sector
• Expanded access to safe abortion care, with 25,535 services provided in 2025, including 14,472 induced abortion services and 11,063 post-abortion care (PAC) cases, bringing the cumulative result to 66,738 services by the end of the year. • Strengthened PAC contraceptive uptake, with 19,801 women and girls adopting a contraceptive method following abortion care in 2025, representing an uptake rate of 78%. • Improved facility readiness and sustainability, with 27 health facilities assessed under the graduation framework and 24 already scoring above the 75% graduation threshold, showing strong progress toward institutional ownership of abortion services. • Expanded clinical mentoring network, training 32 new clinical mentors and refreshing 23 existing mentors, thereby reinforcing quality improvement and continuity of technical support across supported provinces. • Advanced the abortion self-care agenda, with 366 community-linked actors trained in SMA/ASC approaches and the first 9 trained pharmacists already providing support in Niassa, laying the foundation for broader implementation. • Improved the enabling environment for rights-based SRHR, reaching 293 institutional actors through VCAT, of whom 267 (91%) showed improved knowledge, attitudes, and intentions regarding SRHR.
Outcome 2: Humanitarian agencies have enhanced capacity to take evidence-based action to protect SRHR before, during, and after humanitarian crises
• Strengthening integration of SRHR into humanitarian preparedness and response, including incorporation of SRHR and SGBV actions into contingency plans in Marromeu and Dondo districts, and at the provincial level in Sofala, along with the training of 480 humanitarian actors, of whom 413 (86%) improved their knowledge.
Outcome 3: Communities reduce the prevalence of harmful gender norms and cultural practices, increase support for SRHR, and refer people to safe SRH services
• Built a stronger and more sustainable community network, with 374 SRHR advocates (activists) trained, 577 godmothers and traditional healers sensitized/trained, and implementation through 4 local partner organizations. • Generated strong community-to-service linkage, with 8,850 referrals made to SRHR services in 2025, including 6,303 referrals for family planning, 1,463 for safe abortion services, and 1,084 for SGBV services.
Outcome 4: A national movement for SRHRled primarily by women and young peopledemands accountability from government leaders on SRHR and SGBV, and resists threats to progress
• Reinforced a functioning national SRHR movement, with project-supported CSOs implementing 172 advocacy actions in 2025 and contributing to 3 policy advances and 8 public statements or declarations demonstrating greater accountability and ownership of SRHR.
